item.description:
Asobi 1.0 (build 2208) Nov 9, 2026

  • Playlist actions on a right-click. The playlist's More menu could vanish the moment it opened. Its items (Import Timeline, Save As, Trim to In and Out, Clear Trim, Auto-Pair) are now in a Playlist section when you right-click the playlist's footer, a movie's header or any row.
  • Closing a floating panel brings it back. Closing a floating Notes, Playlist or Grade window puts it back in the side panel and shows it, instead of leaving it hidden behind another tab.
Earlier updates

1.0 (build 2205) Nov 9, 2026

  • Menus that closed by themselves. Since 2199, menus and popovers in the window (the playlist's More, the color chip) could close the moment they opened, during playback or a busy review. Fixed. Edit ▸ Undo is plain "Undo" again; ⌘Z still takes back the last mark or playlist change.
  • Progress header. The Notes column's Progress view now reads "26 of 27 shots noted · 11 agency, Nov 8" and fits the column instead of being cut off.
  • Studio Tutorials: the Frame.io round with the agency now has step-by-step figures.

1.0 (build 2199) Nov 9, 2026

  • As on this Mac. A new first choice in the color chip's Footage menu: Asobi leaves the color alone and the picture looks as it does in Preview or QuickTime Player. Stills, and movies from outside the shot folders that nobody has set a color for, start this way.
  • Rejoining a big review. A Mac could fail to join or rejoin a review with a lot in it ("Message too long") while the browser joined fine. Fixed.
  • Sort ▸ Cut Order. Puts every cut movie's shots back together in the edit's order. The shots of one cut can no longer be unlinked from each other.
  • Undo for the playlist. ⌘Z takes back the last playlist change as well as the last mark: adding, removing, moving, sorting, pairing, linking, Set Kitsu Shots, split, join and rename. Edit ▸ Undo says which.
  • Dragging in the playlist. Hold a clip over a row to pair them; a drag that only passes over rows moves the clip, and says where it will land.
  • A new studio tutorial: a round with the agency on Frame.io, for coordinators and producers.

1.0 (build 2191) Nov 9, 2026

  • A Kitsu tab in Notes. The comments on the shot's Kitsu tasks, with their status, drawn frames and replies. Pick one task, several or every task; see the whole movie shot by shot; right-click to answer in a progress note, open in Kitsu or mark addressed.
  • Yours alone. On to start on the studio's Macs, off on any other licence (Settings ▸ Interface). Guests in a review never see it, and it never goes into a report.

1.0 (build 2186) Nov 9, 2026

  • Bring Back knows who said it. Frame.io doesn't give the names of guests on a share, so Asobi reads them off the share's own page: notes now say Art or Madeline, not Frame.io. Bring Back again to put names on comments brought back before.
  • The agency's drawings come back as marks on the frame they drew on.
  • Also post them to Kitsu now puts each comment once on its shot's Compositing task, with the drawn frame attached and the status kept, as well as in its agency notes.
  • The Progress view shows the agency's latest comments under the shot on screen, a count on the others, and an Agency chip to show them on every shot.

1.0 (build 2175) Nov 6, 2026

  • Movies no longer look lifted on a Mac. A reel or clip made for a Rec.709 screen is now tagged gamma 2.4, the curve the viewer shows, so QuickTime Player, Finder and Safari show it as the review looked. Before, mid-grey came up from 128 to 145. The pixels are the same; only the tag changed.
  • Choose the cuts in a Whole Session Reel. The save dialog lists each cut with a box. A grade or edit reference (Grade or Ref in its name) starts unticked, so the movie you matched against stays out. The session remembers your choice.

1.0 (build 2172) Nov 6, 2026

  • Color, Media and Conform, sorted by the job. Each menu groups what you're doing under a small heading (Color: Grade, Match the color, Versions, LUTs and CDLs; Conform: Bring in a cut, Edit the shots, Edit Ref, Send it out, Plates), and every command has one home. The Playlist's right-click menus follow the same groups.
  • Set Kitsu Shot. Which Kitsu shot a shot is (it was Match Shots to Kitsu), from a shot's right-click or Conform ▸ Edit the shots. "Match" now always means color: Match Color to ▸.
  • One Split at Playhead, one Join with Next Shot, for any shot, whether it came from a cut file or a movie.

1.0 (build 2165) Nov 6, 2026

  • LUTs carry a shot's whole color. Generate LUTs now bakes each shot's grade, looks and match together, for every shot with a correction or a match. The index says what each holds.
  • Use a shot's LUT again. Each generated LUT is kept with its shot. In a new conform, right-click the movie ▸ Use Each Shot's Latest LUT (or one clip ▸ Use Shot's Latest LUT) and each shot takes its own.
